_comment: CASE 3A -- PARTIAL PARTICIPATION, LP (multipath) leg. mini_2gpu_2nic (4 hosts x 2 GPUs = 8 GPUs, each GPU carrying its OWN 100Gbps NIC into its leaf, intra-host 200Gbps through hsw, 2 leaf + 2 spine, 16 fine nodes) with 6 of the 8 GPUs active: [0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. Same active set as case 2C, different host interior -- that pairing is the whole reason this case exists. Here a passive GPU owns a NIC, so it is not just a relay, it is EXTRA EGRESS for its active twin; on 2C's shared-NIC host the same passive GPU adds nothing.
_known_limitation: KNOWN LIMITATION, DOES NOT TRIGGER HERE. The MILP under-charges delivery time on a cut-through path when a link is too slow to clock a whole chunk out in one epoch: it pays the store-and-forward cost (1 epoch + beta) once at the first GPU->switch hop and charges later fabric hops only propagation delay, so it credits 1 + beta(FIRST hop) instead of the correct 1 + max(beta over the legs used) = ceil(chunk / min bandwidth along the path). This topology's links are UNIFORM -- 100Gbps GPU NICs and 100Gbps leaf-spine uplinks -- and the epoch is one chunk on a 100Gbps link, so every link's epoch_capacity is exactly 1 chunk, beta is 0 everywhere, and the under-charge has nothing to bite on. Verified for this file. The non-uniform partners (cases 1A, 2B, 2C on the 50Gbps-uplink topologies) DO hit it at their pinned 0.08 s epoch and say so in their own _known_limitation; the reported makespan here is trustworthy, theirs is not.
_participation: active GPUs [0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]; passive GPUs [1, 7]. Node map (class-major, declaration order): 0/1 = srv0.gpu0/gpu1, 2/3 = srv1, 4/5 = srv2, 6/7 = srv3; 8-11 = srv0-3.hsw; 12/13 = leaf0/leaf1; 14/15 = spine0/spine1. srv0+srv1 on leaf0, srv2+srv3 on leaf1, so leaf0 serves participants {0, 2, 3} and leaf1 serves {4, 5, 6}. Passive GPUs still forward; they only drop out of the demand tensor (teccl/solvers/demand.py::_demand_sources). num_chunks 1 means one chunk per (src, dst) PAIR and the chunk axis is widened by the ACTIVE count, so this is 6 x 5 = 30 chunks of 1 GB.
_expected: T* = 0.4 s = 5 epochs, set by the LEAF CUT with half an epoch lost to the ceiling. Cross-leaf demand is {0,2,3} x {4,5,6} = 9 GB per direction against 2 x 100Gbps = 25 GB/s, i.e. 0.36 s = 4.5 epochs, rounded up to 5. A NEAR-MISS worth not mistaking for a second bound: gpu0 and gpu6 are each the ONLY active GPU on their host, so 5 GB through their own 100Gbps NIC would be 5 GB / 12.5 GB/s = 0.4 s -- exactly the ceiling -- which means a schedule that never relays can still hit 5 epochs. It is NOT an independent lower bound, because each of them has a PASSIVE TWIN with its own idle NIC to relay through (gpu0 -> hsw at 25 GB/s -> gpu1 -> gpu1's NIC), so the honest per-host egress figure is 5 GB / 25 GB/s = 0.2 s. gpu2..gpu5 are slacker still at 4 GB each, their intra-host peer chunk riding hsw and never touching a NIC. COMPARE WITH 2C: same participation, same 9 GB cut, but twice the fabric width, so 0.4 s against 2C's 0.8 s -- a clean 2x, which is what the shared NIC costs under this placement. THE MULTIPATH CHECK: 9 chunks per direction over 5 epochs do not fit on one 100Gbps uplink (that is 5 GB), so both spines must be loaded in any optimum; what is LP-specific is the per-PAIR fan, so check that individual 1 GB demands split across spine0 and spine1 rather than merely the aggregate balancing. THE PASSIVE-RELAY CHECK -- the interesting one: at 5 epochs gpu0's own NIC carries its 5 chunks exactly, so the relay through passive gpu1 is not NEEDED and objective_type 6's relay tier should suppress it (expect no relay in the solved schedule). Force it to appear by pinning epoch_type 3 / epoch_duration 0.04: the LP then reaches the true 0.36 s cut bound = 9 epochs, but gpu0's own NIC can only deliver 12.5 x 0.36 = 4.5 GB of its 5 GB, so 0.5 GB MUST detour through the passive twin's NIC. That detour is the thing partial participation makes available and full participation does not, and 0.36 s is unreachable without it. the MILP partner must NOT be run on a 0.04 s clock for comparison: halving the epoch is exactly what forfeits this topology's immunity -- every link drops to 0.5 chunks per epoch, beta becomes 1 everywhere, and the cut-through under-charge described in _known_limitation starts to bite, so its reported makespan there would be optimistic. Compare routings at 0.04 s if you like, but take the timing from the LP or from simulation.
_epoch_note: epoch_type 2 (SLOWEST_LINK) with epoch_duration -1 resolves to 0.08 s = 1 GB / 12.5 GB/s, the 100Gbps NIC, which on this variant is also the leaf-spine uplink rate. The same value the full-participation pair on this topology uses, so all four files are read on one clock. It does NOT divide the binding 0.36 s cut bound -- see _expected for how much that costs and how to recover it.
_symmetry_note: symmetry true is SAFE under partial participation: orbit averaging verifies every candidate permutation against the DEMAND matrix as well as the capacity matrix (symmetrize.py::preserves_demand), so an automorphism mapping an active GPU onto a passive one is rejected -- srv0's gpu0<->gpu1 and srv3's gpu6<->gpu7 both go, which matters MORE here than on 2C because those twins are genuinely interchangeable in the graph (each owns its own identical NIC) and only the demand gate distinguishes them. What survives is srv1's gpu2<->gpu3, srv2's gpu4<->gpu5, the spine swap, and the leaf swap (0<->6, 1<->7, 2<->4, 3<->5).
_hierarchical_note: hierarchical is false, but unlike the shared-NIC variant it need not be: this .topo marks its 4 hosts as cells (their GPUs own their own external links, so _build_cell accepts them). The flat solve is kept as the GROUND TRUTH at 16 fine nodes so that a hierarchical run on this same active set has something to be validated against; expect a hierarchical makespan at or ABOVE the 0.4 s here, and note the coarsening must carry the passive set up (teccl/hierarchy/abstract.py maps a cell to a coarse passive only if its representative fine GPU is passive), so a partially-active cell is NOT coarse-passive -- worth checking explicitly before trusting a hierarchical number on this input.
_topology_note: The topology comes from the .topo DSL file; topo_file SELECTS it, so TECCLSolver.get_topology builds a DslTopology and `name` is only the free-form label for output filenames and the Gurobi log. The path is relative to the repo root.
